Subject: Activation pathway & short-term capacity guardrail for Cerulean Bank (Go-live May 15)

Team —

Quick background: Cerulean Bank (Elaine Campbell, Procurement looped) is ready to sign the MSA, but their security and ops teams have one conditional ask that impacts our delivery timeline: they want a documented activation pathway that includes a limited-time capacity guardrail and a way for us to guarantee peak month performance for the first 90 days of production. This is a deal-closing dependency (estimated ARR $2.1M).

What Cerulean specifically needs:
- A per-deal soft-reservation that ensures they can burst to 2x committed capacity for up to 6 production windows per month for 90 days.
- An operational runbook and escalation flow for failover to our fallback model variant and cross-region routing.
- Audit/logging visibility for every routed request during the ramp.

Asks:
1) Product: can we approve a scoped feature/flag ("activation-pathway") that allows a temporary soft-reservation and enables the runbook? If yes, what are the acceptance criteria and are we comfortable shipping this as an opt-in deal-level control?
2) Eng (Dev): can you assess implementation effort and risk for a short-term "soft-reserve" toggle that sits on top of existing burst pools (no permanent infra changes)? Please include test/data needs.
3) CS (Marissa): will validate the runbook with Cerulean and own the ops checklist.

Timing: Cerulean expects production readiness (not necessarily fully automated) by 2027-05-15. We have the signed LOI pending the one-page activation plan plus MSA redlines.

I attached the draft MSA, a proposed activation plan spreadsheet, and a sample traffic profile the customer shared.

This is high-leverage — happy to jump on a quick 30m sync if it helps.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

Subject: Re: Activation pathway & short-term capacity guardrail for Cerulean Bank (Go-live May 15)

Vanessa — thanks for the write-up and the artifacts. High-level notes from infra/runtime perspective:

- Feasibility: We can implement a deal-level "soft-reserve" on top of the existing burst pools. Implementation approach would be a lightweight policy layer that: (a) tags requests for the deal, (b) prioritizes those requests up to the configured burst window, and (c) emits accounting metrics to the same telemetry pipeline. No kernel/runtime changes required for initial scope.

- Risks: risk of noisy neighbors if other customers also burst simultaneously; need a throttling backstop and clear SLO exemptions for the 90-day window. Also need to ensure KV-cache affinity isn't violated when routing to fallback variants.

- Rough effort estimate: 2 engineers (one backend, one runtime infra) for ~3 sprint-weeks (about 3–4 calendar weeks with QA). If we compress, could do an MVP in ~2 calendar weeks by scoping automation out and doing some manual ops steps for initial launch.

- Data needed to validate: representative traffic profile (thank you for the sample), expected p95/p99 token rates, and any slow endpoint examples. Also we need acceptance criteria from Product for what "success" looks like (latency thresholds, failure budget for the window).

Proposed mitigation/workaround: We can use an existing canary routing + manual shift policy to cover the first activation while we push the soft-reserve flag. That buys time and reduces dev scope for the immediate date.

I'll volunteer to pair with Product on acceptance criteria and can scope a minimal feature toggle PR this week if leadership signs off on the timeline.

Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Runtime
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

Quoted: Attached traffic_profile_sample.json reviewed — looks like three peak windows per week with median token sizes of 1.6k.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-26 09:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Activation pathway & short-term capacity guardrail for Cerulean Bank (Go-live May 15)

Thanks — I'll own customer ops and verification. A few clarifying items from Cerulean's side:
- They want the runbook steps documented end-to-end (who kicks, who monitors, escalation contacts at Redwood).
- They require ad-hoc audit exports for the first 30 days (logs showing routing and model variant decisions) — acceptable as a temporary service add-on.
- They will accept manual escalation to a regional standby pool for the first two weeks if that's faster than a toggled automation.

I'll draft the runbook template and a one-page verification checklist for go/no-go (latency p95 < 350ms for the primary model under soft-reserve, error rate < 0.5% over 1h windows). If Product/Eng can provide the feature toggle and a single test endpoint with test tokens, I will run the PoC with them and Cerulean next week.

I'll also ping procurement to finalize the MSA redline that references the temporary SLO exceptions.

Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Quick update after legal/procurement call with Cerulean this afternoon: they signed the LOI contingent on our one-page activation plan and the runbook. Procurement asked for explicit dates and a DocuSign link for the MSA redline.

Product/Eng: Can we commit to the compressed path (manual ops + minimal toggle) for an initial activation slot on 2027-05-12? Dev, you said we could do an MVP in ~2 weeks if we accept manual steps — that aligns to the ask.

If Product is okay with shipping the scoped toggle as a deal-level opt-in and documenting the runbook, I will send the DocuSign this evening and lock the go-live window with Cerulean. This is a $2.1M ARR anchor — recommend prioritizing.
